title: A Standard for the Transmission of IP Datagrams on Avian Carriers

hero.subtitle: The legendary April Fools' RFC - IP datagrams carried by homing pigeons

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Published on April 1st, 1990, RFC 1149 is one of the most beloved documents in Internet history. It specifies a method for transmitting IP datagrams using homing pigeons as the physical carrier medium.

While written as humor, RFC 1149 is a legitimate document in the RFC series. It was even implemented and tested on April 28, 2001, by the Bergen Linux User Group in Norway, achieving a 55% packet loss rate and round-trip times of 3000-6000 seconds.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Avian carriers can provide high delay, low throughput, and low altitude service. The connection topology is limited to a single point-to-point path for each carrier, used with standard carriers, but many carriers can be used without significant interference with each other, outside of early spring.

Bandwidth
Depends on the weight capacity of the carrier and the storage medium. A pigeon carrying a microSD card could theoretically transfer terabytes per trip.
Latency
Homing pigeon speed averages 50 mph (80 km/h), giving a latency measured in hours for typical distances.
Packet Loss
Susceptible to hawks, cats, weather, and other environmental factors. The Bergen test recorded 55% packet loss.

sections.title: Frame Format
sections.content:
The IP datagram is printed on a small scroll of paper, in hexadecimal, with each octet separated by whitespace. The scroll of paper is wrapped around one leg of the avian carrier.

Frame Format
The IP datagram is printed, on a small scroll
of paper, in hexadecimal, with each octet
separated by whitestuff and blackstuff.

The scroll of paper is wrapped around one
leg of the avian carrier.

A band of strapping tape is used to secure
the datagram's edges.

Multiple scrolls may be carried by multiple avian carriers for load balancing. However, out-of-order delivery is common and the upper-layer protocols must handle reassembly.

sections.title: Implementation
sections.content:
The specification addresses several practical implementation concerns for deploying IP over avian carrier networks.

Audit trails are automatically generated by the carriers, though interpretation requires ornithological expertise. Intrusion detection is provided by the carriers' natural territorial instincts.
